title: Rabbi Simlai Divura
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit ch. 3, halakhah 5: Rabbi Simlai Devora said to him: "And at Your word I did, and at Your word I did."

The statement also appears at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:1: “Rabbi Simlai Devira said to him: ‘At Your word I did.’” Korban HaEdah explains that his name was Rabbi Simlai Devira. With all due respect, the plain sense is as in Vayikra Rabbah 22:9: Rabbi Simlai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, told him, as the verse says, “At Your word I did.” Pnei Moshe also explains it this way. Hyman takes this to refute the suggestion that Rabbi Simlai was called Devira because he expounded “At Your word I did.”

notes.text: Hyman disputes whether Devira is a surname at all, taking the letters as part of the divine-command explanation. Divura, Devora and Devira are retained as the reported forms rather than merged into a new identity.

The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 22:9 directly has Rabbi Simlai explaining a divine command to Elijah, “at Your word.” The Jerusalem Talmud surname readings and the exact Korban HaEdah and Penei Moshe explanations remain separately reported by Hyman; the parallel is not an identity admission.
